items.title: Louis Armstrong: Jazz Casual Interview, 1964-07-10
items.q: when you were playing second cornet to him... I never wanted to do that in Oval Joe... after I left Joe, 1924

ctx.x: Now did you get, in this band, when you were playing second cornet to him, did you get to play solos all by yourself too? Oh, very subtle.

There were like one or two records, I think it was chimes, blues, or something like that. But I never wanted to do that in Oval Joe. Did you sing at all? No. That came later? Yeah. Because he knew I was singing, but the main thing was to kind of play with him. And I was singing in a little quartet and he knew all of that, you know.

Was there any vocalist with the band? No, no vocalist. But then you made records shortly after that. After that, yeah. With vocalists, with Bessie Smith. Yeah. But that was when I went with Fletch Henderson, after I left Joe, 1924. I thought we could play one of the records by Ma Rainey that you played on, as an example of the kind of blues of that period and the blues singers and the way in which you worked with them. This one is called Countin' the Blues by Ma Rainey with the accompaniment by Louis Armstrong,…
